review.finding: No asynchronous stepping or per-frame awaits. Native arena/scope ownership and the independent reference replay remain synchronous. Two compiler modules have one-time isolated reference imports.
review.action: Preserve engine, solver, compiler search, WASM artifacts and frame accounting byte-for-byte.

review.area: Producer, evaluation and research worker startup
review.finding: Independent dynamic imports and authored/aligned input loads were awaited serially.
review.action: Group independent loads with Promise.all, preserving selected compiler roots and input/identity validation. Synchronous CPU work still runs on the same thread; no CPU-parallelism claim.

review.finding: savedCell wrapped synchronous filesystem reads and a synchronous Map lookup in promises for every case.
review.action: Make savedCell and loadState synchronous; retain lazy resolution for remeasurement and deterministic case order.

review.finding: Overlay-data generation waited for ride export and audio mux although it consumes the original spec, track and report.
review.action: Run overlay preparation alongside the dependent ride/mux chain. Await all settlements before composition or cleanup so a failed sibling cannot delete active writers outputs.

review.finding: The checksum request waited for the entire JSON download; optional video metadata was fetched twice.
review.action: Overlap bytes/hash and checksum retrieval, reuse the probed response, and check cancellation before publishing the verified object.

review.finding: Music waited for native preparation, video metadata waited for music, and jobs waited for library loading.
review.action: Overlap independent loading while retaining selection tokens, immediate rejection handling, checksum verification and scrub-only recovery after audio failure.

review.finding: Independent report/label resources and audio/analysis loads were serialized.
review.action: Start together; retain progressive report rendering and optional-resource fallbacks.

review.finding: Every static request awaited three async route misses.
review.action: Dispatch by API namespace and serve static assets directly; preserve API guards and HTTP range handling.

deliberateOrdering: Compiler, judge and native replay CPU work uses synchronous stateful engines. Promise.all would not parallelize that CPU work.
Evaluation/render workers already use bounded process pools. Their inner job loops preserve resource limits.
Performance arm order, warmups, measured rounds and compileWorker calls remain serial for comparable measurements.
Frame rendering, muxing produced video, reading generated files, checksumming post-write artifacts, saves before reloads and publication after validation are dependent operations.
Research/report loops that replay or render one ride at a time remain bounded; cached specification imports do not warrant loading entire datasets concurrently.
Readiness polling and mirror export waits are retained; they synchronize external renderer state and were not proven unnecessary by this audit.

controlledLatency.kind: Controlled delayed-I/O diagnostic, not end-to-end production or physics performance

sources.baseline: async function checked(url,signal,digest){const r=await fetch(url,{signal});if(!r.ok)throw new Error(`Artifact unavailable (${r.status})`);const bytes=await r.arrayBuffer();if(!digest){const sum=await fetch(url+'.sha256',{signal});if(!sum.ok)throw new Error('Missing artifact identity');digest=(await sum.text()).trim();}const actual=await sha256Hex(bytes);if(actual!==digest)throw new Error('Artifact checksum mismatch');return JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(bytes));}

limitations: Latency results use an artificial 80 ms delay on each loopback response. They establish overlap for verified artifact loading, not end-to-end application, rendering, compiler or physics speedups.
Browser loading tests use synthetic signed JSON and generated PCM audio, and stub native drawing to isolate scheduling. The dashboard uses the actual spec view with audio substituted.

The existing full saved-collection browser check could not launch its default Playwright revision; the expected generated collection is also absent locally. The new loading tests ran with the installed Chromium executable.
Render concurrency tests control subprocess completion and validate dependencies, error cleanup and publication. A full production video was not rendered in this audit.
